lines.japanese: 今日は日曜日。
lines.english: Today was Sunday.

lines.japanese: マルチネスとアリスでもいじって暇を潰そうかと思ったけど、やつらはちょうどお巡りさんに怒られて露店を畳みはじめたところだった。
lines.english: I'd thought I might kill time by pestering Martinez and Alice, but a cop was already chewing them out, and they had begun packing up their stall.

lines.japanese: 今日もあのガード方面から聴こえてくるジェンベの音。ちょっと気になったけれど、さすがにもう関わりたくないと思う気持ちの方が強かった。
lines.english: The djembe was sounding from the direction of that underpass again today. I was a little curious, but not wanting anything more to do with it won by a mile.

lines.japanese: さて、どうすっかな。
lines.english: Now, then. What to do?

lines.japanese: 今日は日曜日。現場も休みだから特別することはない。
lines.english: Today was Sunday. The site was closed, so there was nothing in particular I had to do.

lines.japanese: 俺はパイプベンチに腰掛けて、ヤナポリ広場から聞こえてくる音を大小問わず無遠慮に耳へ放りこんだ。
lines.english: I sat on a pipe bench and shoved every sound from Yanapoli Plaza into my ears, the loud ones and the quiet ones alike.

lines.japanese: 広場でいちばん大きな音は、ギャル男たちに言いよられてギャハギャハ笑う強めなギャルたちの笑い声だ。
lines.english: The loudest sound in the plaza was the raucous laughter of the flashy, hard-edged girls being hit on by equally flashy young men.

lines.japanese: およそ日本人とは思えない派手な色の髪。長い爪にはラメやら石やらが貼りついてる。この街にもこういうねーちゃんたちの集まりはいくつかあって、それぞれサークル活動みたいな真似もしているらしい。
lines.english: Their hair came in gaudy colors no Japanese person could have been born with. Glitter and rhinestones clung to their long nails. This city had several groups of women like them, and apparently each ran something resembling a social club.

lines.japanese: 遊んどけ遊んどけ。若いうちに遊んどけ。
lines.english: Go have fun. Have all the fun you can while you're young.

lines.japanese: ギャルとギャル男が交わす下心に満ちた交渉合戦、その愉快な駆け引きをラジオ代わりに、俺は柳木原の夜を愉しんでいた。
lines.english: The girls and guys haggled back and forth with desire written all over them. I listened as if it were a radio show and enjoyed the Yanagihara night.

lines.japanese: 数分後、交渉は成立したみたいだ。男女揃ってぞろぞろ移動を始める。幸いなことに女性陣はひとり残らず、孤独な俺がちっとも嫉妬を覚えなくて済む御面相だった。
lines.english: A few minutes later, the negotiations seemed to be complete. The men and women moved off together in a herd. Fortunately, every last woman had the sort of face that spared a lonely man like me from even a twinge of jealousy.

lines.japanese: むしろ物好きな男性陣の勝利を祝って、やつらの背中に目潰しピースをおくりたい。
lines.english: If anything, I wanted to salute the adventurous men's victory by flashing an eye-gouging V-sign at their backs.

lines.japanese: けれどにーちゃんたち御用心。刺があるのは綺麗な薔薇だけじゃない。あんな凶器みたいな爪で目潰しなんか喰らったら大変なことに──
lines.english: But watch yourselves, gentlemen. Pretty roses aren't the only things with thorns. Take an eye-gouge from nails like those deadly weapons and you'd be in serious—

lines.japanese: 「だーれだっ！」
lines.english: “Guess who!”

lines.japanese: <8>\「あいいいっ！」
lines.english: “Aiiii!”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、うそ正解！　なんでなんでー？　なんで隼人君、声だけで私って分かんの！？」
lines.english: “What? No way, you got it! How? How'd you know it was me just from my voice?”

lines.japanese: 「声じゃねーよ。そんなひとの光を奪える爪してンのは、俺の知ってる中じゃ鳳かおまえぐらいなんだよ」
lines.english: “Wasn't your voice. The only people I know with nails that could rob a man of his sight are you and Naru.”

lines.japanese: 俺は視界をふさぐ邪魔な手を引きはがした。掴んだままの手首を引きよせて、その鋭利な指先を確認する。白地にラメがまぶされていた。
lines.english: I tore the obstructing hands from my eyes. Still gripping one wrist, I pulled it close to inspect the sharpened fingertips. White polish, dusted with glitter.

lines.japanese: 「てめ、なんだこのオサレ凶器。爪切れ、爪」
lines.english: “What the hell are these stylish weapons? Cut your nails.”

lines.japanese: そう言って香田の手を投げすてると、やつは憮然とした口調で反抗した。
lines.english: With that, I tossed Koda's hand away. She protested in an aggrieved tone.

lines.japanese: 「えー？　何なん、そのいきなり命令形ー。散々ときめかせといてそんなん、マジ落ちるんですけどー」
lines.english: “What? Why jump straight to ordering me around? You get my heart pounding and then pull that? What a letdown.”

lines.japanese: 「もともと上がってねーだろ。こっちは１ミリもときめかせた覚えねーんだよ」
lines.english: “You were never riding high enough to be let down. I haven’t made your heart flutter a single millimeter.”

lines.japanese: 「そっかぁー……こーゆーネイル、隼人君の趣味じゃないんだぁー……」
lines.english: “Oh... So nails like these aren't your thing, Hayato...”

lines.japanese: 香田は十本の指を折りまげて、閉じたり開いたりしていた。
lines.english: Koda curled and spread all ten fingers, over and over.

lines.japanese: なんかさっきから会話が成立してない気がする。
lines.english: Somehow, it felt as if this conversation had never connected in the first place.

lines.japanese: 「までも、男の子と女の子じゃカワイイの基準ちがうもんね。仕方ないよね」
lines.english: “Still, boys and girls have different standards for what's cute. Can't be helped.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Right.”

lines.japanese: 俺は適当な相槌を打って、擦れ違いの会話をとりあえず終わらせた。
lines.english: I gave her a perfunctory grunt and brought our two passing monologues to a close.

lines.japanese: 「つーかおまえ、なんなわけ。なんか用。用がないなら眼科医だけ紹介してさっさと帰ってくんねーかな」
lines.english: “Anyway, what are you doing here? You want something? If not, could you introduce me to an eye doctor and hurry on home?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょおー！　も、いきなり何その態度ー」
lines.english: “Heeey! What's with the attitude all of a sudden?”

lines.japanese: 「いきなりじゃねえよ、俺ずっと前からこんな態度だよ」
lines.english: “There's nothing sudden about it. I've always treated you like this.”

lines.japanese: 鷲介みたいに愛想ふりまいてりゃ、そりゃいいことはたくさん待ってるかもしれない。でもその代わり面倒も増える。
lines.english: Sure, scattering smiles everywhere like Shusuke might leave plenty of good things waiting for you. It also meant more trouble.

lines.japanese: １０回笑うたびに１回泣かなきゃならないのだとしたら、俺は生涯で９回も笑えれば充分だ。
lines.english: If every ten laughs meant I had to cry once, nine laughs would be enough to last me a lifetime.

lines.japanese: 「なーん、そんな悪い子ぶっちゃってさー。隼人君、むかし私が絡まれてるとこ助けてくれたじゃん」
lines.english: “Aww, acting like such a bad boy. You saved me when those guys were hassling me before, remember?”

lines.japanese: またその話か。
lines.english: That story again.

lines.japanese: それはもう半年以上も前……いや、もっと前だったか。ほとんど俺自身の記憶からは抜けている。香田が何度も繰りかえし語るから、そういう「史実」として頭の片隅に残っているだけだ。
lines.english: That had been over half a year ago... No, longer, maybe. It had almost fallen out of my own memory. It remained tucked into one corner of my mind as established ‘historical fact’ only because Koda retold it so often.

lines.japanese: たしか香田がタチの悪いおっさんに絡まれてたから、偶然通りかかった俺がちょいと速めのパンチをちらつかせて追いはらった、その程度のなんてことないイベントだ。
lines.english: As I remembered it, some nasty old guy had been hassling Koda. I happened by, flashed a pretty quick punch to scare him off, and that was that. A trivial little event.

lines.japanese: それまで香田とは、ろくに互いの名前も知らないレベルの間柄だった。いまにして思えば、やつが馴れ馴れしく下の名前で俺を呼ぶようになったのはあれ以来だったかもしれない。
lines.english: Until then, Koda and I had barely even known each other's names. Come to think of it, that might have been when she started calling me by my first name with such easy familiarity.

lines.japanese: 「そう、私の中の隼人君の印象、あのとき一変したんだよねー。それまでは、なんか怖いけど面白いやつーみたいな。でもあんときからは、なんか怖いけど面白くて優しくて超カッコいいやつー、みたいな」
lines.english: “Right. That completely changed the way I saw you. Before, you were this scary but funny guy. Afterward, you were this scary but funny and kind and super-cool guy.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　てめ、ふざけんなよ。ハードボイルドが優しいわけねーだろ。勝手に俺のプロファイリングしてんじゃねえよ。おまえに俺の何が分かるっつーんだよ」
lines.english: “Huh? Don't screw with me. A hard-boiled man isn't *kind*. Quit profiling me without permission. What the hell do you know about me?”

lines.japanese: 「きゃはは、ほんとは優しいくせして、照れてやんの。ばーかばーか」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha! You're kind and you know it. Look at you getting embarrassed. Idiot, idiot.”

lines.japanese: 「何その罵声。俺を誉めたいのか貶したいのか、はっきりしてくんない」
lines.english: “What kind of insult is that? Could you decide whether you're praising me or putting me down?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、両方？　愛憎あい半ばするってやつ？」
lines.english: “Mm, both? Love and hate in equal measure?”

lines.japanese: 「あーあ、なんで私、隼人君なんか好きになっちゃったのかなー」
lines.english: “God. Why did I have to fall for somebody like you?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ。馬鹿だからじゃね」
lines.english: “Beats me. Maybe you're an idiot.”

lines.japanese: などと平静を装っていつも通りの返しをしたものの、俺はその実かなり気が滅入っていた。
lines.english: I gave her my usual answer and affected perfect calm. In truth, my spirits had sunk considerably.

lines.japanese: こいつ、どさくさに紛れて好きとか言いやがった。
lines.english: She had slipped in that she *liked* me while my guard was down.

lines.japanese: いままでどれほど好意的に振るまっていても、その言葉だけは言わないできたのに。
lines.english: However openly affectionate she had been until now, she had always stopped short of saying that one thing.

lines.japanese: あーあ。やめてくれよ、そういうの。本気か冗談か知らねーけど、無理だから俺には。惚れた腫れたの青い春なら、森里とかその辺としてればいいじゃないか。
lines.english: Oh, hell. Don’t do that to me. I didn’t know whether she meant it or was joking, but I couldn’t handle it. If she wanted all that youthful romance, she could have it with Morisato or somebody like him.

lines.japanese: 「ああそうだ、おまえには言っとくわ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. There's something I ought to tell you.”

lines.japanese: 突きはなす優しさ。万一やつが本気で言ってるのだとしたら、俺も男だ、本気で答えてやる義務があるだろう。
lines.english: The kindness of pushing her away. On the off chance she meant it seriously, then as a man, I owed her an equally serious answer.

lines.japanese: 「俺、たぶん近いうちいなくなるから」
lines.english: “I'll probably be gone before long.”

lines.japanese: 香田は声にならない声を漏らした。
lines.english: Koda let out a sound that never became a voice.

lines.japanese: 「え……なに？　なにが……？」
lines.english: “What...? What do you mean...?”

lines.japanese: 「どこ行くことンなるかは分かんねーけど、すげえ遠いとこ行って、たぶんもう帰ってくンのは無理だと思う」
lines.english: “I don't know where I'll end up, but it'll be a long way away. I probably won't be able to come back.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　え？　なんで？」
lines.english: “What? What? Why?”

lines.japanese: やつは笑ってる。くだらない冗談だと思ってるんだろう。あるいは好意に対する拒絶かと。
lines.english: She was smiling. She must have thought it was a stupid joke. Or else a rejection of her feelings.

lines.japanese: 「家の事情っつうか、まあ、そんなようなアレで」
lines.english: “Family circumstances, I guess. Something like that.”

lines.japanese: 俺は遠まわしに、しかし俺なりの誠意で答えた。死神が迎えに来てるから、なんて答えるよりはよっぽどマシだろう。
lines.english: I answered obliquely, but with all the sincerity I knew how to give. It was a damn sight better than telling her the Grim Reaper had come for me.

lines.japanese: もし香田が俺に夢見るような幻想を持ってるのだとしたら、だとしたら尚更そんなものはさっさと摘んでしまうべきだ。
lines.english: If Koda harbored some dreamer's fantasy about me, that was all the more reason to nip it in the bud.

lines.japanese: 俺は真実いずれ消えてなくなる存在。片やおまえらは、命長けり恋せよ乙女だコノヤロウ。
lines.english: The truth was, sooner or later I would vanish. You people, though? Life is long—fall in love, girls, goddamn it.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、俺そろそろ行くわ」
lines.english: “Well, I should get going.”

lines.japanese: こんなとこにいたら青春が伝染る。さっさと帰ってハードボイルドの磨きなおしだ。
lines.english: Stay here too long and I might catch youth. Better get home and polish up my hard-boiled act.

lines.japanese: 「え、えーっ！？　ちょちょちょ、待ってよーう、ねーえ」
lines.english: “Wha—wait, wait, wait! Come ooon!”

lines.japanese: 亜衣が俺の腕を掴んでにじり寄る。うぜえ。あの甘ったるい香水の匂いが鼻に──
lines.english: Ai caught my arm and edged closer. Annoying. The cloying scent of her perfume filled my—

lines.japanese: ──あれ、匂わねえな。今日は香水つけ忘れか。どうでもいい。
lines.english: —huh. No smell. Had she forgotten her perfume today? Whatever.

lines.japanese: 「まだいいじゃん。隼人君、道路工事のバイト始まる時間、まだでしょー？」
lines.english: “You can stay a little longer. Your roadwork shift doesn't start yet, right?”

lines.japanese: 「う……よく覚えてんな、そんな細かいこと」
lines.english: “Uh... You remember details like that?”

lines.japanese: 俺の観察日記でも付けてるのか、こいつ。
lines.english: Was this girl keeping an observation journal on me?

lines.japanese: 「だっていま私、隼人君がこの辺ぶらついてる時間に合わせてこの辺ぶらついてたんだもん」
lines.english: “Because I timed my wandering around here to match when you usually wander around here.”

lines.japanese: 実地観測までかよ。フィールドワーク、っつうかストーキングじゃねーか。こえー冗談──
lines.english: Field observations too? Forget fieldwork; that was stalking. Terrifying joke—

lines.japanese: ……え、冗談だよな？
lines.english: ...Wait. It *was* a joke, right?

lines.japanese: 「ね、暇なら私の買い物つきあってよ」
lines.english: “Hey, if you're free, come shopping with me.”

lines.japanese: 「やだ」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、バイトの前になんか用事あんの？　便利屋の方の仕事とか？」
lines.english: “Oh, do you have something to do before work? A job for the handyman business?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、暇。暇だけどおまえの付き合いはやだ」
lines.english: “No, I'm free. I'm free, but I don't want to go with you.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、なんでー」
lines.english: “What? Why?”

lines.japanese: なんでって……聞くかな、そういうこと。フツーここまで断れたら、尻尾まいてすごすご逃げねえ？
lines.english: Why...? She really had to ask? Once somebody rejected you this thoroughly, didn't a normal person tuck tail and slink away?

lines.japanese: 俺に真似のできないそれは、こいつの強さだ──
lines.english: That strength of hers was something I could never imitate—

lines.japanese: ──なんてな。嘘だろ。それなりに傷付いてんだろ。分かってんだよめんどくせえ、こいつさっきから泣きそうな目ぇしてんじゃねーか。
lines.english: —yeah, right. What a load of crap. Of course she was hurt. I knew it, damn it. She'd looked ready to cry this whole time.

lines.japanese: 「あっ、そーだ！　亜衣ぽん、いいこと思いつきー！」
lines.english: “Oh, I know! Your girl Ai just had a brilliant idea!”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあな」
lines.english: “See you.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょおおおー！　聞いてよう！」
lines.english: “Heeey! Listen to me!”

lines.japanese: しがみつかれた。
lines.english: She latched on to me.

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 振りほどいてから仕方なく向きなおる。
lines.english: I shook her off, then reluctantly turned around.

lines.japanese: 「んとね、私がお客として成田工務店に依頼すんの。買い物するから付いてきてくださいって」
lines.english: “Okay, so I hire Narita Construction as a customer. My request is: accompany me while I shop.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえが……？」
上半身を引いて、目の前の自称客を値踏みした。こいつ、そんな金持ってんのか？
lines.english: I leaned back and appraised the self-declared customer before me. Did she even have that kind of money?

lines.japanese: いや、持ってたとして、それを徴収していいのか。たかが買い物の付き合いで、知ってるやつ──しかも年下の女から金を取るって、なんかソレ逆援助交際くせえぞ。ヘタしたら条例に引っかかりそうだぞ。
lines.english: No—even if she did, could I take it? Charging somebody I knew, and a younger girl at that, just to go shopping with her would make me sound like a paid date. At worst, it might even run afoul of an ordinance.

lines.japanese: 「そんな疑わしい顔すんなしー。報酬ならちゃんと出すよ？　ごはん一回分」
lines.english: “Quit looking at me like that. I'll pay you properly, okay? One meal.”

lines.japanese: そんだけかよ。成田工務店、１時間毎９００円（交通費込み）なんですけど。
lines.english: That was it? Narita Construction charged nine hundred yen an hour, transportation included.

lines.japanese: まあ、でも、メシ一食ぐらいなら逆に気兼ねはしなくて済むな。犯罪臭もしないし。いや、しかし社会人として学生におごられるのはちょっと不名誉な気も……。
lines.english: Still, one meal was little enough that I wouldn't feel bad accepting. It didn't smell like a crime, either. Though as a working adult, letting a student treat me felt mildly disgraceful...

lines.japanese: 「どうよ。亜衣ぽんに軽く雇われてみ？」
lines.english: “Well? Wanna let your girl Ai hire you for a bit?”

lines.japanese: 「悩んでるくらいなら行こーよ。歩いてる間に考えればいーじゃん」
lines.english: “If you're gonna agonize over it, let's just go. You can think while we walk.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、いやごめん、やっぱ俺……」
lines.english: “Mm, no, sorry. I still—”

lines.japanese: 「いーじゃんいーじゃん、ちょお高級料理おごっちゃうよ」
lines.english: “Come on, come on. I'll buy you something super expensive.”

lines.japanese: 「……マジか」
lines.english: “...Seriously?”

lines.japanese: けっきょく俺は、一食分のエサとそよ風のような力に引かれるまま歩きはじめた。
lines.english: In the end, one meal's worth of bait and the force of a passing breeze drew me into motion.

lines.japanese: そのあと俺たちは、この前見たケータイショップなんかに張りついたり、相変わらずトッピングしかない亜衣の日本語で騒ぎたてたりしながら通りを歩いた。
lines.english: After that, we wandered the avenue, lingering at the phone shop we’d seen before and making a racket in Ai’s Japanese, which as usual was all verbal toppings and no substance.

lines.japanese: 俺の旅立ち宣言は、どうやら面白くもない冗談として処理されたみたいだ。並んでバカ話をしている間、やつはその件について言及してこなかった。
lines.english: Apparently my announcement that I would soon leave had been filed away as an unfunny joke. As we walked side by side trading nonsense, she never brought it up again.

lines.japanese: なんでもいいやと思った。
lines.english: Whatever. I decided it didn't matter.
